reading.body:
Privacy and AI hiring in this sample is mostly a legal and governance function, not an engineering one: five of six postings are counsel, advisory, or program roles, and only one is a research engineering job.

The titles cluster around the same work. Two Harvey postings are Privacy and AI Counsel for EMEA, neoshare wants a Data Protection and AI Governance Advisor, Goodwin Recruiting is filling a Privacy, Cybersecurity and Technology Attorney role, and Figure wants a Technical Program Manager for Security and Privacy. OpenAI's Research Engineer, Privacy is the only posting in the set that sits on the technical side. The employers are a mix of AI companies, a robotics company, a staffing firm, and a European employer, which suggests the demand is not confined to one segment.

Geography splits evenly, with München, London, and Dublin on one side and Grand Rapids, San Francisco, and San Jose on the other. Three of the six are flagged remote, including both Harvey counsel roles and the OpenAI engineering role. Only one posting discloses pay, the Goodwin attorney role at $240,000 to $325,000 per year, so the set cannot support any claim about compensation across the function.

Six postings on a single build date is a small sample, and it is drawn from aggregators and company career boards rather than a census, so it shows what these roles look like and not how many exist or whether the count is rising. The data contains nothing about compute, data centers, or power, so it cannot speak to the grid constraint on AI scaling. What it does show is that the compliance layer around AI is being staffed with lawyers and program managers, and that layer grows with deployment rather than with hardware.
